claim: For the characteristic-three reduction of the integral Igusa-quartic equation, the projective Jacobian singular scheme has a length-\(6\) embedded component at \(P=(1:\cdots:1)\), the common vertex of the \(15\) pair-partition lines.

correctness.rationale: The gradient criterion on the hyperplane reduces to equality of the six partial derivatives. The multiplicity argument proves the reduced support is the 15 pair-partition lines. The exact Gröbner and direction-point calculations give the Hilbert-series difference of length six; generic reducedness and S6 symmetry localize the embedded contribution at P.

evidence: The inspected article states that it works in characteristic different from 2 and gives the quartic equation and 15-line support. It does not give the Jacobian ideal's Hilbert series or the length of an embedded excess.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior statement covers the reduced singular support, including characteristic 3, but does not state the scheme-level length-six contribution. The claim is deliberately narrowed to that additional structure.
